audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Cassiopeia all seven stages, against a 54.16% Garen win rate over 1119 games, while the page's own whys[2], whys[3] and the mid paragraph all say levels 3-5 are Garen's kill window. The packet chart agrees: Garen at Level 3 and Levels 4-5. The full layer also sits at FAV 8/10 with carry threat 9/10.
audit.why: The chart contradicts the win rate, the packet, and the prose printed beside it. The mirror (cassiopeia__garen) hit the same wall and left the chart alone believing the length band would reject a 'Cassiopeia' to 'Garen' edit — that belief is wrong, side fields are enum-exempt, so the flip is made here.
audit.corrected: Levels 3 and 4-5 flipped to Garen in both layers, proposed as one chart group. diff set to EVEN, diffRating 6/10 and carryRating 6/10 to match the settlement the mirror already made on its own side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Petrifying Gaze appears three times with no cooldown, and Miasma is quoted at '12s' in report[5]. Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 — 12s is not a value it ever has. Twin Fang's real shape (0.75s cooldown, 40 mana a cast) was never given either.
audit.why: The 24s rank-1 Miasma is the step-up trigger for the entire 3-5 window, and it was being reported at half its true length. Twin Fang's 40-mana spam cost is exactly why she is beatable at level 3 and not at first item.
audit.corrected: Miasma corrected to 24s at rank 1 in report[5] and mid; Petrifying Gaze given its 120s rank-1 cooldown in whys[4] and spikes[1]; Twin Fang's 0.75s / 40-mana shape in spikes[2] and mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json W cd 24/22/20/18/16, E cd 0.75 cost 40, R cd 120/100/80

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive property of Petrifying Gaze — it stuns only enemies FACING her and merely slows anyone with their back turned — was stated once in passing and never as the instruction it should be. Separately, three fields say Miasma's grounding stops Garen's gap-close.
audit.why: Turning your back is the single highest-value input in this matchup and it deserves to be the headline, not a clause. The grounding claim is the risky one: Riot's text says grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities, and Decisive Strike is a self-buff rather than a dash, so whether it is denied is not answerable from the data.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] now leads with the facing rule and the cost of a missed 120s ultimate. Every claim that Miasma grounds Garen's engage was replaced with what the kit does state — poison, slow, kiting — rather than asserting or denying the grounding interaction. Twin Fang's healing added as the Grievous Wounds trigger in wants.you[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json R text, W text, E heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice on this matchup.
audit.why: Every green light here is Miasma's downtime, and there was no line telling the reader to wait for it.
audit.corrected: mid now says to step up as Miasma goes down, 24s at rank 1, with the mana constraint on Twin Fang as the second half of the window.

edits.before: Track Cassiopeia’s Miasma (12s): Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Cassiopeia’s Miasma (24s at rank 1): slows and poisons the ground she wants you to cross. Step up the moment it is spent.

edits.before: At 2 her W grounding and Twin Fang keep you out.
edits.after: At 2 Miasma slows and poisons you out of range.

edits.before: At 6 Petrifying Gaze stuns your engage and flips the lane.
edits.after: At 6 Petrifying Gaze, 120s, stuns you only if you face her.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze stuns you if you face her, letting her kite your engage and stack Twin Fang damage; her poison DPS wins the extended fight.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing her — turn your back and you are slowed instead. It is 120s at rank 1, so the miss costs her two minutes.

edits.before: Once she has mana and Malignance/Liandry her poison-plus-Twin-Fang DPS out-damages you and she kites your Q-slow with W grounding.
edits.after: Once she has mana and Malignance her poison plus Twin Fang, a 0.75s-cooldown spam at 40 mana a cast, out-damages you in any long fight.

edits.before: Full AP Cassiopeia melts you with sustained poison, grounds your gap-close with her W, and her R hard-CCs your commit — a losing extended fight.
edits.after: Full AP Cassiopeia melts you with sustained poison and heals off every Twin Fang, and Petrifying Gaze answers your commit — never take the long fight.

edits.before: At levels 3-5 you flip it: your Q gap-close and silence get you onto her while she is still mana-starved, and your E shreds her squishy frame faster than her poison can answer. This is your kill window — use it.
edits.after: At levels 3-5 you flip it: step up as Miasma goes down, 24s at rank 1, and your silence lands before Twin Fang, which she cannot spam at 40 mana a cast this early. This is your kill window — use it.

edits.before: From level 6 on she pulls back ahead — Petrifying Gaze stuns your engage if you face her, her W grounds your slow, and her poison-plus-Twin-Fang DPS out-sustains you once she has mana and AP items, so avoid extended fights and turn away from her ult.
edits.after: From level 6 on she pulls back ahead — Petrifying Gaze stuns you only if you face her, and her poison plus Twin Fang out-sustains you once she has mana and AP items, so refuse extended fights and turn your back the instant she ults.

edits.before: Buy Merc Treads and an early MR item to survive her poison
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds — Twin Fang heals off every tick

edits.before: Ground your Q-slow engage with Miasma (W) and kite
edits.after: Drop Miasma on your step-up and kite the poison

notes: The packet's suspectNames entry for wants.foe[1] ('Land Petrifying Gaze') is a FALSE POSITIVE — that is the correct name of her R and the line is right, so I left it. UNVERIFIED, deliberately left out of the page: whether Miasma's grounding denies Decisive Strike. Riot's text says grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities; Decisive Strike is a move-speed self-buff with no dash, and nothing in the data settles whether it counts. Three fields previously asserted that it does — I removed the assertion rather than replace it with the opposite claim.
